Lenacapavir is a long-acting antiretroviral drug. It targets the HIV-1 capsid—the protein shell that encloses the virus’s genetic material—and disrupts the virus’s ability to multiply. (accessdata.fda.gov)
On June 18, 2025, the U.S. FDA approved lenacapavir under the brand name Yeztugo for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of getting HIV-1 through sex. It’s approved for at-risk adults and adolescents who weigh at least 35 kg (77 lb) and test negative for HIV-1 before starting. After the starting doses, it’s given by injection every six months. (accessdata.fda.gov)
The 2025 approval was for prevention. Lenacapavir had already been approved in 2022 as Sunlenca for use with other antiretroviral drugs to treat certain adults with drug-resistant HIV-1. (fda.gov)
